page: Microsoft Azure L16aos_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The hardware configuration is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 11519 GB of Premium Storage capable capacity, though it does not feature any integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is highly competitive, reaching the top 10% tier in Geekbench text processing benchmarks. Multi-core operations, database transactions, and Redis SET operations perform in the average range. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is a notable bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 25% at 36.77 GB/sec. Large-model LLM inference is also limited, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L16aos_v4 offers a dense allocation of local storage and memory relative to its compute core count, making it a viable option for workloads that require substantial local data caching without the premium cost of high-core-count instances. It is highly suitable for database hosting, text processing pipelines, and moderate-scale web serving. The lack of GPU acceleration and poor large-model inference speeds make it unsuitable for deep learning training or large-scale AI workloads, but it remains a strong candidate for storage-heavy enterprise applications.
